text:
Maya (design): quick check on the Create Resource form. two items we need to settle: 1) how to surface validation for very dense/batch forms 1 rows+? inline errors on each field vs a compact error summary at top? 2) required field signal 1 asterisk alone or explicit 'Required' label for a11y and clarity?
Jordan (pm): for batch-create use-case i prefer top summary + anchors to first error. reduces scan noise when there are many rows. inline is great for single-item flows.
Sam (eng): perf note: inline per-field error nodes multiply DOM updates during validation passes. summary-only can be lighter for huge forms. we can lazy-render inline hints on focus to balance both.
Kai (a11y): asterisk alone is ambiguous for some screen readers. recommend explicit visible text 'Required' that is also programmatically connected (aria-describedby or aria-required). if we keep asterisk visually, include a visually-hidden explanatory string for AT.
Maya (design): copy tone: current messages are terse ("Name required"). propose friendly but concise "Please enter a name for this resource." which helps users understand why.
Jordan (pm): agree on friendlier copy. Also question on destructive flows: typed confirm modal vs inline undo toast. which to default to?
Sam (eng): typed confirm is safest for irreversible customer-data deletes but is more friction. if we can offer soft-restore we should prefer undo toast for quick recoverability.
Kai (a11y): typed confirm needs careful focus management and ARIA instructions. screen reader users should be told the exact phrase to type and the field should be focused programmatically. otherwise it's confusing.
Maya (design): proposed pattern: for forms show compact error summary with count + anchor links. reveal inline error copy when user focuses the field or after they attempt submit. for required markers show asterisk visually but render "Required" text in a visually-hidden span and expose it via aria-describedby so it's read aloud. also show a tooltip or helper text on hover for sighted users.
Jordan (pm): sounds good. for destructive: typed confirm for one-off permanent deletes, undo toast for bulk deletions if backup retention exists. we should document thresholds (e.g., >100 rows = bulk path).
Sam (eng): implementation idea: reuse .sr-only and aria-describedby patterns in our form component. lazy mount inline error nodes on focus to reduce initial DOM cost. I can prototype this in the component lib.
Kai (a11y): add aria-live="polite" to the summary container so AT users get notified after submit. and avoid auto-focusing the summary; instead allow users to tab in. if we anchor, ensure the anchor receives focus only when activated.
Maya (design): microcopy options for summary header: "We found X problem(s) with this form" vs "Please fix these errors". which resonates?
Jordan (pm): "We found X problem(s) with this form" is less accusatory and clearer.
Sam (eng): agree. also include short rationale in inline helper: "Required 1 needed to provision resources." for a handful of critical fields.
Maya (design): quick reaction poll: :one: inline-eager (show inline errors as they appear) vs :two: summary-first (show top summary initially, reveal inline on focus). react with :one: or :two:.
RedwoodBot: New reactions added. :thumbsup:
Kai (a11y): vote :two:. summary-first gives an AT-friendly sweep and reduces cognitive overload for complex forms. just ensure discoverability via keyboard and screen reader navigation.
Jordan (pm): tally looks like :two: leads. let's run a small usability session with 6 participants (mix of power users and novice) to validate.
Maya (design): i'll mock two variants (summary-first with inline-on-focus, and inline-eager) and upload a short prototype. will tag @Sam for feasibility check and @Kai for a11y signoff before we ship copy tweaks.
Sam (eng): I'll try to get a minimal prototype by EOD and measure render perf with 200-row dataset.
Kai (a11y): i'll review keyboard flows and screen reader text. remember to test on NVDA and VoiceOver.
Maya (design): thanks all 1 will post mocks tomorrow. :sparkles:
